title.narrative: WGG- Building Inclusive Movements and Alliances in Rwanda

description.narrative: It is a strategic platform for activists to participate in and learn about differing viewpoints, form creative alliances and highlight issues that are generally considered to be beyond the purview of women’s rights and gender justice.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

Annual podcast episodes and annual advocacy campaign for 16 days of violence against women

(i) Radio talk show on public understanding of cultural social norms that sparks sexual and gender based violence for women and girls, consent, intimate partner sexual violence, a topic often overlooked in public discourse. It introduced clear language, legal context and cultural relevance, helping listeners recognize that consent is essential in all relationships. (ii) 3 podcasts - women engagement in technology, GBV, women in leadership. Guest speakers AD team and Institute Alumni.

Annual podcast episodes and annual advocacy campaign for 16 days of violence against women

On the occasion of 16 days of activism, 25 women and girls, both with and without disabilities, had created awareness and developed a shared action against elimination of sexual and Gender based violence. Celebrated IWD led by the young women in the informal settlement of Gisagara that was attended by 50 participants. One YW, Yvonne Nkaka Uwizya was featured in a post on disability empowerment by Newyork Times where she did advocacy on women with disability.
